ai.description: This 10–16 cm snake resembles an earthworm with a glossy, cylindrical body. It is uniform dark brown or grey with a blunt, rounded head and a tiny terminal spine on the tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Brahminy Blind Snake is best identified by its uniform, glossy dark-brown to black scales and a tiny, spine-tipped tail, lacking the distinct patterns of other species.
ai.habitat: The Brahminy Blind Snake inhabits moist, loose soil in tropical gardens, forests, and agricultural lands, ranging from sea level up to 1,500 meters in the Indian subcontinent.
ai.behavior: The Brahminy blind snake is primarily nocturnal and fossorial, spending most of its life burrowing through soil or leaf litter in search of ant and termite eggs.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Indotyphlops braminus* is an obligate parthenogen that reproduces without males. They lay clutches of 1–8 eggs, typically during the monsoon season in India.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Brahminy blind snake is widespread across the Indian subcontinent, occurring from sea level up to 2,000 meters in diverse habitats across nearly all Indian states.
